back2basics.concept: Electoral Rolls and Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are official lists of eligible voters maintained by the Election Commission. Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a process to update these rolls, including adding new voters and deleting names of those who are ineligible, to ensure accuracy before elections. Voters must verify their inclusion to exercise their right to vote.

2026-11-14-pm-0e85893b69.deck: The Congress party launched a website, Iamvoterakshak.in, enabling voters to verify if their names were deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and to apply for restoration. This initiative is part of Congress's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities, emphasizing voter rights and transparency in the electoral process.

back2basics.text: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution to protect certain laws, especially those related to land reforms and social justice, from judicial review. Laws placed in this schedule cannot be challenged in courts for violating fundamental rights, thus providing them immunity from legal scrutiny. This mechanism is often used to safeguard affirmative action laws from being struck down.

2026-11-14-pm-93cdc55a13.deck: Karnataka government has recommended including its law enhancing SC/ST reservation in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution to shield it from legal challenges. This move raises important constitutional questions on reservation laws and the scope of Ninth Schedule protection, relevant for UPSC aspirants studying social justice and federalism.

body.label: Law details
body.text: The Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services Under the State) Act, 2022, increases reservation for SCs from 15% to 17% and for STs from 3% to 7%.
